pr_title: Bluetooth: Controller: Fix missing chain PDU channel indices
pr_body:
Fix missing population of channel indices for Extended Advertising Chain PDUs.

Fixes #79671.
pr_comments:
> Code looks OK, but it's concerning that there are no tests for this. Should/can one be added?

Will try to check if there are unit tests that expose the channel indices. bsim tests do not have DF support.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Controller: Wrong channel index in connectionless AoA
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

I am working on direction_finding_connectionless_rx/tx samples using Nordic nrf52833 and nrf5340. I noticed that with `PER_ADV_EVENT_CTE_COUNT` set to `5` on the tx side, CTE reports from the rx side are like 
```
PER_ADV_SYNC[0]: [DEVICE]: EF:BB:1A:FA:87:19 (random) synced, Interval 0x03c0 (1200 ms), PHY LE 2M
success. Periodic sync established.
Enable receiving of CTE...
success. CTE receive enabled.
Scan disable...Success.
Waiting for periodic sync lost...
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 24, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -690
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 0, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -760
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 0, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -760
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 0, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -760
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 0, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC not OK, CTE Info OK, RSSI -760
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 36, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -410
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 0, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -380
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 0, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -380
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 0, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -380
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 0, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -380
PER_ADV_SYNC[0]: [DEVICE]: EF:BB:1A:FA:87:19 (random) sync terminated
Periodic sync lost.
```
They are basically a random selected channel `N` followed by four `0` for each CTE train. As far as I know, channel number within a single train should be the same in Zephyr. Please correct me if not.

I also tested it with a ST processor as the TX (not running on Zephyr), with RX remained unchanged, and `PER_ADV_EVENT_CTE_COUNT` was set to `4`. As you can see from the log message below, channel index were 4 different numbers for the ST part (ST has a different channel selecting strategy). That means the `direction_finding_connectionless_rx` sample was working as expected and it was `direction_finding_connectionless_tx` that might have some issue.
```
Waiting for periodic sync lost...
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 31, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -480
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 7, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -470
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 32, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -480
CTE[0]: samples count 45, channel ID 18, cte type AOA, slot durations: 2 [us], packet status CRC OK, RSSI -480
PER_ADV_SYNC[0]: [DEVICE]: A0:AC:7E:00:00:00 (public) sync terminated
```

**To Reproduce**

Zephyr version: 3.7.99
SDK: zephyr-sdk-0.16.8
TX board: nrf52833 devkit
RX board: nrf5340 devkit

For TX side: build `direction_finding_connectionless_tx` and flash
```
west build -p always -b nrf52833dk/nrf52833 samples/bluetooth/direction_finding_connectionless_tx -DEXTRA_CONF_FILE=overlay-aoa.conf
west flash
```
For RX side: 
1. add channel ID print to `cte_recv_cb` in `direction_finding_connectionless_rx`
```
static void cte_recv_cb(struct bt_le_per_adv_sync *sync,
			struct bt_df_per_adv_sync_iq_samples_report const *report)
{
	printk("CTE[%u]: samples count %d, channel ID %u, cte type %s, slot durations: %u [us], "
	       "packet status %s, RSSI %i\n",
	       bt_le_per_adv_sync_get_index(sync), report->sample_count, report->chan_idx,
	       cte_type2str(report->cte_type), report->slot_durations,
	       packet_status2str(report->packet_status), report->rssi);
}
```
2. build and flash

**Impact**

AoA calculation uses channel index for wavelength calculation. There would be bias if incorrect.

**Additional context**

The bug was first found on nRF Connect SDK, then I switched to Zephyr Project and was able to reproduce the problem. There are some details I posted in Nordic Forum https://devzone.nordicsemi.com/f/nordic-q-a/114492/direction-finding-chan_idx-of-cte-sent-in-single-periodic-advertising-train, which I didn't get an answer from Nordic but could be some useful FYI.

review_comments: Do we really need to guard prototypes?
as it is declared static, compiler expects it to be used or warns about.
I guess the static function is guarded because it access some values that are guarded then?
it is not referenced if the `CONFIG_BT_TICKER_EXT_EXPIRE_INFO`  and `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_ADV_AUX_PDU_BACK2BACK` are disabled. As no values in the aux pointer in the PDU being transmitted are updated.

Yeah, I think this is a sideeffect of the (quite massive) use of `#if` in the controller design :) There was actually a discussion on this in Discord (https://discord.com/channels/720317445772017664/1295816189766795304) about this, but it's way outside the scope of this PR
